19 |\section{Introduction}
20 |Polynomial regression provides a direct setting for studying how model complexity and coefficient regularization affect prediction on observations excluded from fitting. Increasing polynomial degree expands the class of functions a model can represent, while ridge regularization penalizes coefficient magnitude. These choices can affect both approximation error and sensitivity to the available training sample. Greater flexibility may improve prediction when the response depends nonlinearly on the input, but it can also introduce unnecessary parameters when a simpler relationship is adequate. Consequently, training error alone is insufficient for choosing polynomial degree or regularization strength.
